trials.notes: Used the documented WP_HTML_Tag_Processor template-fill pattern almost exactly: seed the known shape, preserve src/alt order by predeclaring attributes, walk tokens to the #text placeholder, call set_modifiable_text(), then return get_updated_html(). No undocumented calls and no _doing_it_wrong records.

All called methods are documented across the two rendered files, and the implementation correctly uses create_fragment(), token walking, set_attribute(), set_modifiable_text(), and inherited get_updated_html(). The only adherence loss is processor choice: this fixed, byte-exact template fill is the Tag Processor use case in the docs; HTML Processor is valid but heavier and not needed for structure here.

Same API pattern as trial-2: documented methods only, correct null guard for processor creation, placeholder text replacement, and get_updated_html() rather than serialize(). It loses a few points for choosing HTML Processor where the docs’ template-building guidance points to Tag Processor.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three passed 7/7 with no doing_it_wrong records. The docs did well on the key contracts this task needed: the Tag Processor "Building markup from a template" section explicitly says to use a literal template, include empty attributes to preserve order, include placeholder text for later replacement, and finish with get_updated_html(). The set_attribute docs explain plaintext input, automatic encoding, boolean handling, and why newly added attributes sort by name. The set_modifiable_text docs explain that ordinary element text lives on #text tokens, empty elements have no replaceable text node, and plaintext captions are encoded rather than parsed as markup. The near-miss was processor selection: two trials used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), likely because they were building an HTML fragment and walking to text. That still passed because the docs state HTML Processor inherits the mutation output path, but the task did not require tree-aware parsing.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md > Overview / HTML Support > Supported elements
doc_gaps.problem: The docs distinguish structural work from flat edits, but they do not explicitly steer readers away from HTML Processor for trusted literal template filling where exact source bytes and attribute order matter.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short cross-reference: for generating or filling a known markup shape with untrusted values, prefer WP_HTML_Tag_Processor plus the template-fill recipe unless browser tree repair, subtree boundaries, or normalized serialization are required.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor copy of set_attribute() documents encoding and boolean values but omits the Tag Processor section about attribute placement and alphabetical ordering of newly added attributes.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Repeat or cross-link the attribute placement contract from WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::set_attribute(), especially that existing attributes keep position and multiple new attributes sort by name.

doc_gaps.problem: One example checks '#text' with get_token_name(), while the surrounding recipe and token-type docs use get_token_type(). Both can work for text nodes, but the mixed pattern invites confusion about which method is the intended predicate.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Use get_token_type() === '#text' consistently in text-node mutation examples, and reserve get_token_name() for tag or node-name checks.
